trigger: Police seized my phone or property
description: What to do if officers take your phone, money, or other belongings.

steps.text: Stay calm. Do not struggle over the item, but do not agree that they can keep it.
Ask why it is being taken and on what legal authority. Your property and privacy are protected (s.44, s.37).
Ask for a receipt or written record listing exactly what was taken.
Note the item, its condition, the officer's name and number, and the station.
Do not share your phone password unless your lawyer advises it; ask on what authority they demand it (s.37).
Property lawfully seized for a case should be documented and returnable; keep any receipt safe.
Call your lawyer or a trusted person to help recover it.

citations.source_name: 1999 Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
